correctness.rationale: For the specified self-inclusive asynchronous minority rule every active vertex flip makes same-color edge energy E nonincreasing. E>=m, equality exactly when each triangle nonmonochromatic; from every E>m state some monochromatic triangle permits a strict peripheral energy decrease. At E=m, for each fixed hub color the m independent edge-neutral peripheral coordinates form P3^m; hub may flip exactly when all m coordinates are corners, with 2^m matching cross-layer edges and therefore one irreducible 2*3^m-state class. Symmetric transition rates 1/(2m+1) imply uniform stationary law; fraction (2/3)^m of corners gives rate (2/3)^m/(2m+1). Starting from stationarity conditioned on one hub layer, union bound on hub crossings gives TV >=1/2-t r_m and lower mixing bound ceil(1/(4 r_m)). Independent exhaustive enumeration m=1..4 recovered energy structure, recurrent connectivity, cross-layer counts and stationary rate. Does not establish any matching upper bound on mixing time.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge originality: older Rouquier–Regnault–Thierry self-inclusive minority analysis has the same update and monotone energy but examines cliques, paths, cycles and tree cases, not the product geometry or windmill bottleneck. Published stochastic-minority bottleneck on K_m,m,m is for a different graph and yields a six-hypercube attractor, not the 2*3^m two-P3^m structure. Synchronous windmill minority results with numerically equal counts are not asynchronous recurrence. No identified publication implies the exact 2^m cross-layer matching, stationary hub-switch rate or F_m bound.
